summary: Modern databases have evolved beyond storage and querying to embed AI/ML capabilities directly into the data layer, eliminating the need to move data to external ML platforms. Vector search has become a foundational feature across all major platforms, with 75% of enterprise AI applications expected to depend on it by 2026 and adoption growing 377% year over year. From Snowflake Cortex AI's text-to-SQL and embedding generation to PostgreSQL's pgvector extension and pgai toolkit, enterprises can now run RAG pipelines, LLM inference, and semantic search natively within their existing database infrastructure.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides a suite of serverless AI functions running natively in the Snowflake AI Data Cloud, including text-to-SQL (Cortex Analyst), embedding generation, classification, sentiment analysis, summarization, and LLM-powered completions. Snowflake Postgres (generally available in 2026) runs natively in the AI Data Cloud and supports pgvector for vector similarity search, allowing teams to unify transactional, analytical, and vector workloads. Cortex Search enables hybrid vector and keyword search over unstructured data, and Cortex Fine-tuning allows custom model adaptation without data leaving Snowflake.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM inference via Cortex AI supports models including Mistral, LLaMA, Snowflake Arctic, and others served serverlessly. Cortex Analyst provides natural language to SQL translation. Snowflake Postgres integrates pgvector for embedding storage and similarity search, and data can be mirrored from Postgres to Snowflake for broader analytics and AI processing.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed by Snowflake credits consumed per token or per function call. Cortex Search and embedding generation consume credits based on volume. Snowflake Postgres pricing follows standard Snowflake compute and storage credit model. No separate infrastructure cost for LLM inference as it is fully serverless.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to build and execute ML models using standard SQL directly inside BigQuery, supporting logistic regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, boosted trees, AutoML, and deep neural networks. BigQuery Vector Search enables semantic similarity queries over embedding columns stored natively in BigQuery tables. Integration with Vertex AI allows BigQuery to call hosted Gemini and other foundation models for text generation, summarization, classification, and embedding creation via remote functions and the ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT SQL functions.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native integration with Google Vertex AI and Gemini model family. ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT SQL functions call Vertex AI endpoints directly from BigQuery SQL queries. Supports Gemini Pro, Gemini Flash, and text-embedding models. Remote functions extend BigQuery to any Vertex AI or Cloud Run hosted model.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training costs are based on bytes processed. Vector Search queries are billed per query and index storage. Vertex AI model calls from BigQuery are billed at Vertex AI token rates in addition to BigQuery compute costs. BigQuery sandbox offers free tier for exploration up to monthly limits.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector similarity search capabilities, enabling storage of high-dimensional embeddings as a native column type and querying via cosine similarity, L2 distance, and inner product. It supports HNSW and IVFFlat indexing for approximate nearest neighbor search and is widely regarded as the lowest-friction path to vector search for teams already running Postgres, handling up to 50 million vectors comfortably. pgai complements pgvector by adding functions to call external LLM APIs (including OpenAI and Ollama) directly from SQL, enabling embedding generation, text completion, and RAG pipeline construction within the database itself.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension allows direct SQL calls to OpenAI, Ollama, and other LLM providers from within PostgreSQL functions and queries. Embeddings can be generated and stored in the same transaction as data inserts. Integrates with Snowflake (via data mirroring) and Databricks environments. Supabase Vector, Neon, and other managed Postgres providers offer pgvector as a first-class feature.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use on self-hosted PostgreSQL. Managed providers such as Supabase, Neon, AWS RDS, and Google Cloud SQL offer pgvector on existing instance pricing with no additional extension fee. LLM API calls from pgai are billed by the respective LLM provider at their standard token rates.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Aurora ML integrates Amazon Aurora (MySQL and PostgreSQL compatible) with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock, enabling SQL-based invocation of ML models for inference without moving data out of the database. Aurora PostgreSQL supports pgvector for vector similarity search natively. Redshift ML allows data warehouse users to build, train, and deploy ML models using SQL via integration with SageMaker AutoPilot, and supports calling Bedrock foundation models for generative AI use cases directly from Redshift SQL queries. Amazon Bedrock integration across Aurora and Redshift enables access to Claude, Titan, Llama, and other foundation models.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora PostgreSQL supports pgvector extension for vector similarity search. Both Aurora and Redshift integrate with Amazon Bedrock for foundation model inference including Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan Embeddings, Meta Llama, and Mistral models called via SQL functions. Redshift ML uses SageMaker AutoPilot for automated model training and deployment.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference calls are billed per SageMaker or Bedrock invocation in addition to standard Aurora instance costs. pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL has no additional extension licensing cost. Redshift ML model training costs are based on SageMaker compute hours. Bedrock model calls from Redshift are billed at Bedrock token pricing rates.

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.ai_feature: Databricks AI: MLflow, DBRX, Mosaic AI, and Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI platform built on the Lakehouse architecture, with MLflow as the open-source standard for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment. Mosaic AI (formerly Databricks ML) offers managed model serving, AI Gateway, and agent frameworks. DBRX is Databricks' own open foundation model optimized for enterprise workloads. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database built into Unity Catalog that automatically syncs embeddings from Delta Lake tables and supports real-time similarity search for RAG pipelines. Databricks integrates with pgvector environments and supports Snowflake data sharing via Delta Sharing.
databases.llm_integration: Native support for DBRX, Llama, Mistral, and other open models via Mosaic AI Model Serving. AI Gateway provides a unified API for routing between internal and external LLM providers including OpenAI and Anthropic. MLflow tracks all experiments and model versions. Databricks Agent Framework enables multi-step agentic AI workflows with tool use and retrieval augmentation over Vector Search indexes.
databases.pricing_notes: MLflow is open-source and free. Databricks platform is billed by Databricks Units (DBUs) consumed by compute clusters. Vector Search is billed per DBU for indexing and query compute plus storage costs. Model Serving is billed per token for provisioned throughput or per DBU for pay-per-token endpoints. DBRX model access is included in Databricks platform subscription.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables semantic search over vector embeddings stored natively alongside operational data in MongoDB collections, using the HNSW algorithm for approximate nearest neighbor queries. It supports filtering vector search results by any MongoDB document field simultaneously, enabling pre-filtered and post-filtered hybrid search without separate vector database infrastructure. Atlas Vector Search integrates with popular embedding providers and LLM frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Haystack, making it a strong choice for RAG applications that need to combine structured document metadata with semantic retrieval in a single query.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas Vector Search integrates with OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, and other embedding providers for generating and storing embeddings. Native connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex enable RAG pipeline construction. MongoDB Atlas also offers Atlas Search (BM25 keyword) that can be combined with vector search for hybrid retrieval. No native hosted LLM inference but integrates via Atlas Functions and triggers with external model APIs.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 and above dedicated Atlas clusters with no separate licensing fee for the vector search feature itself. Costs are driven by Atlas cluster tier (compute and storage). Serverless Atlas instances have limited vector search support. Search indexes consume additional storage billed at Atlas storage rates. Free tier M0 clusters do not support Atlas Vector Search.
